questions.questionText: A person ends south-west of the start after moving 6 m south and then 4 m in an unknown cardinal direction. Which direction could the second move be?
questions.explanationText: South followed by west gives both negative x and y, hence south-west.

questions.questionText: After moving 7 m east, a person moves in an unknown cardinal direction and ends north-east of the start. Which direction must the second movement be?
questions.explanationText: A northward second leg creates positive x and positive y.

questions.questionText: A person walks 5 m north and then 5 m in an unknown cardinal direction, finishing north-west of the start. Find the second direction.
questions.explanationText: The second move must add a westward component while the northward component remains positive.

questions.questionText: A point is 6 units east and 8 units north of O. What distance west must it move to become directly north of O?
questions.explanationText: Its x-coordinate is +6; moving 6 west makes x=0 while y remains +8.

questions.questionText: A point at (−5,7) moves east to become directly north of the origin. How far does it move?
questions.explanationText: It must change x from −5 to 0, requiring 5 units east.

questions.questionText: A walker goes 3 m north and 4 m east. What single direction leads straight back to the start?
questions.explanationText: The final point is north-east of start, so the reverse direction is south-west.

questions.questionText: A vehicle ends 8 km west and 15 km south of base. What is the direct return direction?
questions.explanationText: The outbound displacement is south-west; the reverse vector is north-east.

questions.questionText: A faces east. What smallest clockwise turn makes the person face north?
questions.explanationText: Clockwise from east goes south, west, then north: 270°.

questions.questionText: A faces south-west. What smallest anticlockwise turn makes the person face east?
questions.explanationText: SW→S→SE→E is three 45° anticlockwise steps, or 135°.

questions.questionText: A person travels north and east in the ratio 3:4 and has displacement 20 m. How far east?
questions.explanationText: The 3:4 legs form a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 4; eastward distance is 4×4=16 m.

questions.questionText: Northward and westward legs are in ratio 5:12, with displacement 26 m. Find the westward leg.
questions.explanationText: A 5-12-13 triangle scaled by 2 gives legs 10 and 24.

questions.questionText: A walks twice as far south as east. If the eastward leg is 6 m, what is the final direction from start?
questions.explanationText: The displacement has positive east and larger negative south components, so it is south-east.

questions.questionText: A route has equal north and south movement, but east exceeds west by 9 m. Where is the endpoint?
questions.explanationText: Vertical movements cancel; net horizontal displacement is 9 m east.

questions.questionText: A route has total distance 30 m: 8 m north, 7 m south, 9 m east, and the rest west. How far west is the last leg?
questions.explanationText: The last leg is 30−(8+7+9)=6 m.

questions.questionText: Route A: 10 m east then 10 m north. Route B: 15 m north then 5 m east. Which has greater total distance?
questions.explanationText: Each route totals 20 m.

questions.questionText: Route A ends at (6,8); Route B ends at (9,12). Which endpoint is farther from start?
questions.explanationText: Distances are 10 and 15 respectively.

questions.questionText: Route A: 5 m north, 7 east. Route B: 7 east, 5 north. How do endpoints compare?
questions.explanationText: Order does not change the net vector (7,5).

questions.questionText: Route A travels 12 east and 5 north. Route B travels 5 west and 12 south. Compare displacements.
questions.explanationText: Both magnitudes are 13, but vectors are opposites.

questions.questionText: A loop is 4 north, 6 east, 4 south, 6 west. What is displacement?
questions.explanationText: All horizontal and vertical movements cancel.

questions.questionText: A person walks 10 east, 6 west, and 8 north. What is total distance?
questions.explanationText: Total distance is 10+6+8=24 m; displacement is different.

questions.questionText: For the same route 10 east, 6 west, 8 north, what is displacement?
questions.explanationText: Net vector is (4,8); distance √(16+64)=√80=4√5 m.

questions.questionText: Which route returns to its start?
questions.explanationText: Only the first has zero net horizontal and vertical displacement.

questions.questionText: Which route can end north-west of its start?
questions.explanationText: The first has net 7 north and 3 west.

questions.questionText: Which final direction is possible if a person moves only north and east, at least once in each?
questions.explanationText: Both components are positive, so the endpoint must be north-east; pure north or east would require one component to be zero.

questions.questionText: Two people start together. P walks 3 east and 4 north; Q walks 3 west and 4 south. Distance between them?
questions.explanationText: Their positions are (3,4) and (−3,−4); difference (6,8) has length 10.

questions.questionText: P ends 5 m east of O; Q ends 12 m north of O. Distance P-Q?
questions.explanationText: Difference is (5,−12), a 5-12-13 triangle.

questions.questionText: A is 8 m north of O; B is 15 m west of O. Which direction is B from A?
questions.explanationText: From A to B the vector is (−15,−8), hence south-west.

questions.questionText: C is 6 m south of O; D is 8 m east of O. Shortest C-D distance?
questions.explanationText: Difference components are 8 east and 6 north; distance 10.

questions.questionText: One route totals 30 m and returns to start; another totals 24 m and ends 10 m away. Which has greater displacement?
questions.explanationText: Returning to start means zero displacement; the second has 10 m.

questions.questionText: A person walks 8 north, 15 east, then 8 south. What is displacement?
questions.explanationText: North and south cancel, leaving 15 m east.

questions.questionText: A route goes 5 east, 12 north, 5 west. What is shortest distance from start?
questions.explanationText: East and west cancel; the endpoint is 12 m north.

questions.questionText: A traveller goes 9 south, 12 west, then 9 north. Final direction?
questions.explanationText: Vertical movement cancels, leaving 12 m west.

questions.questionText: Which route has the greatest total distance?
questions.explanationText: Totals are 24, 20, 18, and 17 m.

questions.questionText: Which endpoint is closest to origin?
questions.explanationText: Distances are 5, √37, √34, and 7; (3,4) is closest.

questions.questionText: Which pair is farthest apart?
questions.explanationText: Distances are 9, 6, 5, and √41≈6.4; the first pair is farthest.

questions.questionText: If all moves are due east or west and the endpoint is north of start, what is true?
questions.explanationText: Purely horizontal movement cannot create a northward displacement.

questions.questionText: A route ends south-east. Which net components are required?
questions.explanationText: South-east means positive x and negative y.

questions.questionText: If a path has total distance equal to the magnitude of displacement, which condition is required?

options.text: All movement is along one straight direction without reversal
The path contains a closed loop

questions.explanationText: Equality occurs when no detour or reversal lengthens the route.

questions.questionText: A route has displacement 0 but total distance 40 m. Which statement is true?

options.text: It returns to its starting point

questions.explanationText: Zero displacement means identical start and end points.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O and moves 12 m north, then 5 m east, then 7 m south, then 9 m west, then 4 m north, then 12 m east, then 9 m south. What is the final direction from O?
questions.explanationText: Coordinate tracking gives final displacement (8,0), which is East.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O and moves 15 m west, then 8 m north, then 4 m east, then 11 m south, then 9 m east, then 6 m north, then 3 m west. What is the shortest distance from O?
questions.explanationText: The endpoint is (-5,3); shortest distance is √((-5)²+(3)²)=√34 m.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O and moves 10 m south, then 16 m east, then 14 m north, then 7 m west, then 9 m south, then 5 m west, then 3 m north. What is the final direction from O?
questions.explanationText: Coordinate tracking gives final displacement (4,-2), which is South-East.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O and moves 20 m east, then 6 m south, then 13 m west, then 15 m north, then 2 m east, then 4 m south, then 9 m west. What is the shortest distance from O?
questions.explanationText: The endpoint is (0,5); shortest distance is √((0)²+(5)²)=5 m.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O and moves 18 m north, then 12 m west, then 5 m south, then 20 m east, then 11 m south, then 4 m west, then 2 m north. What is the final direction from O?
questions.explanationText: Coordinate tracking gives final displacement (4,4), which is North-East.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O on a square grid and moves 3 grid units south-west, then 8 grid units north, then 4 grid units east, then 2 grid units south-east, then 7 grid units west, then 1 grid unit north. For a diagonal move, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. What is the shortest distance from O?
questions.explanationText: The endpoint is (-4,4); shortest distance is √((-4)²+(4)²)=√32 grid units.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O on a square grid and moves 5 grid units north-east, then 9 grid units south, then 6 grid units west, then 2 grid units north-west, then 3 grid units east, then 4 grid units north. For a diagonal move, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. What is the final direction from O?
questions.explanationText: Coordinate tracking gives final displacement (0,2), which is North.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O on a square grid and moves 4 grid units south-east, then 10 grid units west, then 7 grid units north, then 3 grid units north-east, then 5 grid units south, then 2 grid units east. For a diagonal move, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. What is the shortest distance from O?
questions.explanationText: The endpoint is (-1,1); shortest distance is √((-1)²+(1)²)=√2 grid units.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O on a square grid and moves 6 grid units north-west, then 8 grid units east, then 3 grid units south, then 2 grid units south-west, then 9 grid units north, then 1 grid unit west. For a diagonal move, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. What is the final direction from O?
questions.explanationText: Coordinate tracking gives final displacement (-1,10), which is North-West.

questions.questionText: A surveyor begins at O on a square grid and moves 7 grid units north, then 3 grid units south-east, then 5 grid units west, then 4 grid units south, then 2 grid units north-east, then 6 grid units east, then 1 grid unit north. For a diagonal move, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. What is the shortest distance from O?
questions.explanationText: The endpoint is (6,3); shortest distance is √((6)²+(3)²)=√45 grid units.

questions.questionText: A is 8 grid units north of B. C is 6 grid units east of A. D is 3 grid units south of C. E is 10 grid units west of D. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is E from B?
questions.explanationText: Using B as (0,0), the statements place E at (-4, 5). Hence E is North-West of B.

questions.questionText: P is 12 grid units west of Q. R is 5 grid units north of P. S is 7 grid units east of R. T is 9 grid units south of S. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is T from Q?
questions.explanationText: Using Q as (0,0), the statements place T at (-5, -4). Hence T is South-West of Q.

questions.questionText: K is 4 grid units south of L. M is 9 grid units east of K. N is 6 grid units north of M. O is 3 grid units west of N. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is O from L?
questions.explanationText: Using L as (0,0), the statements place O at (6, 2). Hence O is North-East of L.

questions.questionText: F is 7 grid units east of G. H is 11 grid units north of F. J is 4 grid units west of H. K is 15 grid units south of J. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is K from G?
questions.explanationText: Using G as (0,0), the statements place K at (3, -4). Hence K is South-East of G.

questions.questionText: R is 5 grid units north-west of S. T is 8 grid units east of R. U is 6 grid units south of T. V is 2 grid units west of U. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is V from S?
questions.explanationText: Using S as (0,0), the statements place V at (1, -1). Hence V is South-East of S.

questions.questionText: B is 9 grid units south of C. D is 4 grid units west of B. E is 12 grid units north of D. F is 10 grid units east of E. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is F from C?
questions.explanationText: Using C as (0,0), the statements place F at (6, 3). Hence F is North-East of C.

questions.questionText: M is 6 grid units east of N. P is 8 grid units south of M. Q is 3 grid units west of P. R is 13 grid units north of Q. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is R from N?
questions.explanationText: Using N as (0,0), the statements place R at (3, 5). Hence R is North-East of N.

questions.questionText: W is 10 grid units west of X. Y is 4 grid units south of W. Z is 15 grid units east of Y. A is 9 grid units north of Z. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is A from X?
questions.explanationText: Using X as (0,0), the statements place A at (5, 5). Hence A is North-East of X.

questions.questionText: C is 3 grid units north-east of D. E is 7 grid units west of C. F is 2 grid units south of E. G is 9 grid units east of F. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is G from D?
questions.explanationText: Using D as (0,0), the statements place G at (5, 1). Hence G is North-East of D.

questions.questionText: H is 14 grid units north of J. K is 5 grid units east of H. L is 8 grid units south of K. M is 11 grid units west of L. For diagonal relations, each grid unit changes both coordinates by one. In which direction is M from J?
questions.explanationText: Using J as (0,0), the statements place M at (-6, 6). Hence M is North-West of J.

questions.questionText: A walks east for 6 minutes at 50 m/min, then north for 8 minutes at 50 m/min. Shortest distance from start?
questions.explanationText: Legs are 300 m east and 400 m north; displacement is 500 m.

questions.questionText: A cyclist rides north for 5 minutes at 120 m/min and west for 5 minutes at 160 m/min. Final direction?
questions.explanationText: Displacements are 600 m north and 800 m west, so the endpoint is north-west.

questions.questionText: A robot moves east and north in distance ratio 12:5. If displacement is 26 m, northward distance?
questions.explanationText: The 5-12-13 triangle is scaled by 2; northward leg is 10 m.

questions.questionText: A person walks 40% of a 50 m route north and the rest east. Final direction?
questions.explanationText: The legs are 20 m north and 30 m east, both positive.

questions.questionText: A drone flies 30 m east, 40 m north, then directly back to start. Total distance?
questions.explanationText: The outward displacement is 50 m; total is 30+40+50=120 m.

questions.questionText: A patrol walks 9 m north, 12 m east, then returns directly. Length of return leg?
questions.explanationText: The return leg equals the 9-12-15 displacement.

questions.questionText: A person facing north makes right, right, left, U-turn, then right turns. Final facing?
questions.explanationText: N→E→S→E→W→N, so the final facing direction is north.

questions.questionText: A point moves 6 NE grid units, 4 south, 9 west, and 1 north. Direction from start?
questions.explanationText: Using NE as (+1,+1) per grid unit gives (6,6)+(0,−4)+(−9,0)+(0,1)=(−3,3), north-west.

questions.questionText: Two walkers start together. A goes 8 east and 6 north; B goes 8 west and 6 south. Direction of B from A?
questions.explanationText: B−A=(−16,−12), hence south-west.
